sent_bad: According to `doc.txt`, satisfaction with customer service interactions drops during the holiday season for two main reasons:

Retailers bring in "20-40% of their annual sales during the weeks leading up to Christmas" (doc.txt), and the document notes that "Q4 is our busiest time of year, and every parameter that impacts a successful customer experience is strained" (doc.txt).

Managers describe the same pattern: "People are buying less thoughtfully so there are more purchase regrets and returns that we have to deal with" (doc.txt), and "During the holidays, customers don't understand how things work as well as our typical customer. We have to spend more time on education and misunderstandings at a time when we're busy anyway" (doc.txt).
In short, the "dip" is driven by the combination of sharply higher ticket volume per agent and a customer base that is more stressed, less experienced, and more prone to purchase regrets and returns.
